function.mechanism: Weak-acid preservative action that inhibits microbial growth (especially molds), with regulatory function categories including antimicrobial and flavoring uses.
common_food_categories: Other foods under GMP use conditions

adi.basis: EFSA 2014 re-evaluation concluded a numerical ADI was not considered necessary for propionic acid and its sodium, calcium, and potassium salts.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA reported no safety concern at reported uses/use levels for E280-E283, while noting local gastric effects at high concentrations.

fda.notes: Affirmed GRAS as a direct human food ingredient; use with no limitation other than current good manufacturing practice; functional uses include antimicrobial and flavoring agent.

adi.basis: Group ADI NOT LIMITED (1973) for propionic acid and calcium/potassium/sodium salts, maintained at the 49th meeting (1997).

concerns.summary: A randomized human crossover study reported acute increases in counterregulatory hormones and endogenous glucose production after calcium propionate challenge; a large prospective cohort also reported associations between several preservatives (including calcium propionate) and type 2 diabetes incidence.
Model-system studies (Drosophila, human lymphocytes in vitro) reported oxidative stress and genotoxicity-related endpoints at tested concentrations.
Zebrafish embryo study reported circadian and developmental/glucose-metabolic perturbations after sodium propionate exposure.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2014 re-evaluation for E280-E283 found no safety concern at reported uses and use levels.
JECFA maintained the group ADI as NOT LIMITED.
US CFR affirms propionic acid as GRAS under GMP conditions.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical EFSA or JECFA ADI value is set for direct exceedance calculations; exceedance cannot be computed in the usual mg/kg bw/day sense from these regulatory endpoints.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory bodies continue to allow use (EFSA no concern at reported uses; US GRAS; JECFA not-limited group ADI), but newer human and mechanistic literature presents non-trivial metabolic and genotoxicity-related signals that justify a cautious mid-tier classification rather than risk-free/limited.
key_factors: EFSA 2014: no safety concern at reported uses; no numerical ADI deemed necessary
JECFA: group ADI NOT LIMITED maintained
Recent human and mechanistic studies report possible metabolic and genotoxicity-related concerns
No IARC carcinogenic classification identified for propionic acid
